mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE changes and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, reducing corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods following a GDPC1 decline, or the correlation between GDPC1 growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals supply chain disruptions, reducing corporate output and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO changes and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth exceeds 3% in a quarter and housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% in the same period, it signals strong economic growth, boosting consumer and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 3% and HOUST growth > 5% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of GDPC1 and HOUST growth on SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% signals accommodative monetary policy, reducing borrowing costs and boosting corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3%, it signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE changes on SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, boosting corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of periods following a RSAFS increase, or the correlation between RSAFS growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
